subject: surgery
title: Malignant Melanoma and Benign Skin Proliferations

steps.tx: Arising from neuroectodermal melanocytes, **malignant melanoma** represents the most lethal of all cutaneous neoplasms. Genetic drivers include activating mutations in the BRAF oncogene, most commonly the V600E substitution in the MAP kinase signalling cascade, alongside NRAS and KIT mutations. Intense intermittent ultraviolet exposure, blistering childhood sunburns, family history, and the presence of dysplastic melanocytic naevi represent the predominant predisposing risk factors.
steps.say: Malignant melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer arising from melanocytes, driven by BRAF V600E and NRAS mutations. Severe blistering sunburns and dysplastic naevi are primary risk factors.

vis.alt: Clinical appearance of an asymmetric pigmented malignant melanoma lesion.
vis.caption: Cutaneous malignant melanoma with asymmetrical architecture and irregular margins. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Bedside clinical screening for suspicious pigmented lesions follows the **ABCDE melanoma criteria**. Lesions are scrutinised for Asymmetry where two halves do not match, Border irregularity with notched or scalloped contours, Colour variegation displaying multiple shades of black, brown, red, or white, Diameter exceeding six millimetres, and Evolution denoting any documented alteration in size, shape, surface elevation, or bleeding.
steps.say: The ABCDE rule helps screen suspicious pigmented lesions: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Colour variegation, Diameter greater than six millimetres, and Evolution in appearance over time.

rows: One half of the lesion fails to match the other
Edges are scalloped, notched, or poorly defined
Hues of tan, dark brown, black, red, and blue
Lesion diameter greater than 6 mm (pencil eraser)
Documented change in size, shape, or symptom

steps.tx: The single most important histological prognostic determinant in primary melanoma is the **Breslow thickness**. Measured with an ocular micrometer, it quantifies the vertical microscopic depth in millimetres from the top of the epidermal granular cell layer to the deepest invading malignant melanocyte in the dermis or subcutis. Survival correlates inversely with Breslow depth, which dictates the necessary surgical resection margins and indications for sentinel node biopsy.
steps.say: Breslow thickness measures vertical tumour depth in millimetres from the granular layer to the deepest melanocyte. It is the single most important prognostic factor in primary cutaneous melanoma.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating microscopic tumor invasion depth across cutaneous layers.
vis.caption: Cross-sectional anatomy of skin layers correlating with depth of tumor invasion. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Historically, microstaging utilised the **Clark level of invasion**, which categorises tumour penetration according to anatomical dermal boundaries. Level one is confined to the epidermis in situ; level two invades into the papillary dermis; level three fills the papillary dermis and abuts the reticular dermis; level four invades between collagen bundles of the reticular dermis; and level five infiltrates into the underlying subcutaneous adipose tissue.
steps.say: The Clark classification defines anatomical levels of invasion from level one in situ within the epidermis to level five invading the subcutaneous fat, complementing Breslow measurement.

steps.tx: Definitive surgical therapy requires **wide local excision** with margins dictated strictly by the Breslow depth confirmed on initial excisional biopsy. Melanoma in situ requires a zero point five centimetre clear margin. Tumours measuring up to one millimetre require a one centimetre margin, tumours between one and two millimetres warrant a one to two centimetre margin, while lesions thicker than two millimetres mandate a two centimetre radical margin down to deep fascia.
steps.say: Wide local excision margins depend strictly on Breslow depth: zero point five centimetres for in situ, one centimetre up to one millimetre depth, and two centimetres for tumours exceeding two millimetres.

steps.tx: To stage regional lymphatic basins accurately, **sentinel lymph node biopsy** is performed concurrently with definitive wide excision. A radiocolloid tracer like technetium-99m and vital blue dye are injected intradermally around the primary biopsy site. The first draining lymph node in the regional basin is identified with a gamma probe, excised, and examined with serial sectioning and immunohistochemistry for micrometastatic disease, indicated for all melanomas thicker than zero point eight millimetres.
steps.say: Sentinel lymph node biopsy maps the first draining lymph node using radiocolloid and blue dye. It is recommended for melanomas thicker than zero point eight millimetres or ulcerated thin tumours.

steps.tx: Differentiating vascular proliferations requires distinguishing benign tumours from vascular malformations, exemplified by **infantile haemangioma**. Appearing shortly after birth as a bright red, strawberry-like plaque, it undergoes rapid cellular proliferation during the first year of life followed by spontaneous slow involution over five to seven years. It stains positively for glucose transporter one protein and responds promptly to oral propranolol therapy when functional impairment threatens vision or airway.
steps.say: Infantile haemangiomas are GLUT-1 positive vascular tumours that proliferate during infancy before spontaneously regressing over several years. Oral propranolol is first-line when treatment is needed.

points: Appears in early weeks of life, not at birth

steps.tx: A rapidly growing, crateriform cutaneous lesion that mimics squamous cell carcinoma is **keratoacanthoma**. Characteristically presenting on sun-exposed skin of elderly individuals, it evolves over several weeks into a firm, dome-shaped nodule with a central plug of keratin debris. Although lesions historically demonstrate spontaneous involution over months leaving a depressed scar, complete surgical excision with clear margins is standard management because histological differentiation from invasive squamous carcinoma is unreliable.
steps.say: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing dome-shaped nodule with a central keratin-filled crater. Because it clinically and histologically resembles squamous cell carcinoma, surgical excision is standard.
